slides.title: Is your short track kit leaving gaps?
slides.sub: Protection from head to ankle, piece by piece

slides.title: Why short track needs cut protection
slides.body: Skaters race in a tight pack with long, sharp blades passing close. A plain base layer, collar or sock offers almost no defence against a passing edge.

slides.title: Cover every exposed zone
slides.caption: Helmet, neck guard, Kevlar undersuit, gloves and ankle socks each cover one part of the body.

slides.title: Higher level, more cut resistance
slides.body: LiveLica uses level 3 fabric for the undersuit and neck guard, and level 4 for the ankle socks, which are labelled to the EN388 standard.

slides.title: Put it on in a fixed order
slides.body: Ankle socks first, then the Kevlar undersuit, boots and blades, race suit and neck guard. Gloves go over the cuff, then the helmet.

slides.title: Three gaps to check every time
slides.body: Throat above the collar, wrist between glove and sleeve, ankle between boot and suit leg. Test them in the low position, not standing up.

slides.title: Juniors: fit now, never buy big
slides.body: A loose undersuit shifts in a slide and a loose helmet moves on impact. Fit protection correctly now and accept some pieces will be replaced.
